newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan committee urges cut in corporate tax rates.
newsitem.headline: Japan committee urges cut in corporate tax rates.

text.p: A Japanese government committee on corporate taxes on Tuesday urged the government to cut corporate tax rates to the level of other nations and to expand the scoop for taxable income.

But at the same time, the committee, which is under the government's tax panel, said Japan was in no condition now to cut the overall tax burden in light of tight state finances, and the fact that companies' overseas investment plans were more determined by other factors, such as exchange rates, than tax levels.
"In the future, it may be possible to discuss easing the tax burden in real terms, but at this moment, the environment is not such as to allow such a thing," the committee said in a report.
Japan's corporate tax rate now stands at 37.5 percent, compared to 35 percent in the United States.
The report, which did not say how much the tax rate should be cut, was submitted and approved by the tax panel on Tuesday.

Panel chairman Hiroshi Kato told reporters it would be possible to include some corporate tax revisions in the annual tax review for the next fiscal year, but if most members thought an overhaul of the system was necessary before that, implementation could be delayed.
The report said the revisions were expected to help revitalise the economy by encouraging new businesses and improving production efficiency, while easing the drop in foreign investment in Japan.
It said it should also stop domestic companies reporting deficits in their accounts to avoid taxes and help solve the problem of Japanese companies' overseas units not returning profits to Japan.
With more and more companies operating abroad, the report stressed the need to work with other countries to devise international rules to establish bases for taxable income.
As one way of broadening the scope for taxable income, the report suggested abolishing tax-deductable reserves, such as those for product guarantees.

It also called for a cut in tax deductions on reserves for retirement allowances, and urged a review of the current system for four other reserves, such as reserves for losses on loans and for the payment of employee bonuses.
A review of special tax measures aimed at alleviating the tax burden for certain companies should be reviewed and taxes on non-profit organisations increased, it said.
The report also recommended assessing the value of financial products using mark-to-market accounting rules.
Taxing companies on a consolidated basis should be studied further before any consideration is given to its introduction, it said.
